messages:
maria_support: FYI — Acme is seeing intermittent 502/503s on hosted inference when using streaming chat. ~10% of streams fail in last 2h. SDK v0.9.3, region=us-west2, model=redwood-large, typical prompt ~8k tokens. Repro steps below. Request-IDs included.

maria_support: repro steps (from customer):
```python
from redwood import Client
cli = Client(api_key=os.getenv('ACME_KEY'))
for i in range(300):
    resp = cli.chat.stream(model='redwood-large', messages=[{'role':'system','content':'...'}, {'role':'user','content':'lorem'*1000}], timeout=60)
    # many clients run concurrently (they use 50 workers)
```
They also said they see socket resets and occasional 524 on long streams.

liam_oncall: @maria_support thanks — can you paste a couple request-ids and the exact error payloads? Also whether they're using the JS or Python SDK (and which transport: http chunked vs websockets).

maria_support: request-ids: r-0a1b2c3d, r-0a1b2c6f, r-0a1b2c90. Errors include "upstream reset" and HTTP 502 with no body, and sporadic "stream timed out (524)". They say they're using python SDK (chunked HTTP streaming) with connection reuse enabled.

oliver_eng_rt: grabbing logs for those IDs. Quick question: are they multiplexing many streaming calls over a single persistent connection or spinning new TLS conns? That pattern matters.

maria_support: they confirmed they reuse a connection pool with keep-alive and pipeline multiple parallel streams over same connection (pool size ~8 per worker).

oliver_eng_rt: :eyes: okay. I'm seeing a pattern in edge-proxy metrics — spikes in active streams per connection correlate with increased socket resets on the upstream side. There's a queue/backpressure signal from the runtime around 15:21 UTC.

emily_solutions: can we reproduce internally with the same concurrency profile? I can spin up a job to mimic 50 workers x 8 concurrent streams each (400 concurrent streams) and the same prompt sizes.

oliver_eng_rt: please do. Also trying to correlate with recent edge config change — yesterday we rolled a keepalive tweak to reduce idle timeouts. Not saying it's the cause but it's in the window.

statusbot: Incident created: INC-2026-1983 — "intermittent 502/524 streaming under high connection multiplexing". Priority: P2.

emily_solutions: repro run started. Using SDK v0.9.3 and default pool settings. I'll push metrics and logs to the incident channel.

emily_solutions: repro confirmed. At ~350 concurrent streams we observe 502 spikes and resets from the edge within 20s of load start. Captured tcpdump shows FINs on keep-alive connections right before upstream request resets.

oliver_eng_rt: that matches the edge proxy behavior I'm seeing — the proxy is pruning connections too aggressively while streams are still active if per-connection active-streams > 6. There's a race where the keepalive/tcp idle detector miscounts active streams when chunked streaming is in-flight, leading to connection eviction and upstream 502s.

liam_oncall: temporary mitigation suggestion for customer: reduce per-worker concurrency to 2-4 streams, or upgrade to SDK v0.10.0-preview which has a client-side change to avoid multiplexing streaming requests on a single connection (it uses multiple sockets instead). Can we confirm that helps?

emily_solutions: tested quickly — with multiplex disabled (one stream per socket) the 502s drop to <0.5% under same load. Also lower concurrency to 200 concurrent streams removes the spike entirely.

maria_support: passing that to Acme: ask them to try SDK v0.10.0-preview and lower pool size while we patch. Also asked for their traffic window for a coordinated test.

oliver_eng_rt: root cause: edge proxy mis-evicts keep-alive connections during long-lived chunked streams under high multiplexing. Fix is a small change to the connection liveness counter and a backoff when eviction occurs during active streaming. I'm prepping a patch.

statusbot: Patch PR: https://git.internal/redwood/edge-proxy/pulls/4821 linked to INC-2026-1983.

oliver_eng_rt: rolling patch to staging now. Plan: staged rollout to 10% of edge nodes 30m, monitor stream 502 rate and connection resets. If green, escalate to full rollout.

liam_oncall: recommend we also apply per-tenant connection hard-limits at the LB to protect shared pools while fix is in rollout. Ops, please add a temporary limit of 100 concurrent streams per tenant in us-west2.

maria_support: customer update: "We've reproduced on our load profile and have a mitigation: use SDK v0.10.0-preview or reduce concurrency. We're deploying a fix edge-side and will notify when rolled out. Recommended temporary limit: max 200 concurrent streams." They replied they can throttle to 200 for the next 24h.

emily_solutions: staging looks good. 10% nodes passed; 502 rate down 98% vs baseline under the synthetic test. Rolling to 50% now.

oliver_eng_rt: full rollout started. Ops has applied per-tenant soft-limits as requested. Monitoring dashboards: stream_502_rate, edge_conn_reset_rate, active_streams_per_conn. All trending down.

maria_support: sent final customer note: patch rolling, suggested SDK upgrade and concurrency tuning, offered a follow-up call to validate. Customer acknowledged and scheduled a test window tomorrow 16:00 UTC.

liam_oncall: postmortem todo: track the edge change that introduced the miscount, add unit tests for active-stream bookkeeping, and run a load test matrix for multiplexing scenarios.

statusbot: Incident INC-2026-1983 status -> monitoring.

oliver_eng_rt: closing loop here — root cause identified and patched, temporary mitigations shared, customer accepted workaround and test window. Will draft a short postmortem and link to PR and dashboards.

maria_support: :thumbsup: I'll follow up with the customer after the validation window and then we can close the ticket. Thanks everyone.
